unit.title: More Letters of the Gurmukhi Alphabet

lesson.title: A New Kind of Sound: ਟ and ਠ
lesson.subject: punjabi

contentBlocks.text: You know fourteen letters now! Today we start a brand-new row with a sound you make in a new way: curling your tongue back. Meet ਟ (tainka) and ਠ (thattha).

ਟ (tainka) and ਠ (thattha) are made by curling the tip of your tongue back and touching the roof of your mouth — try it and feel how different that is from other sounds you've learned! ਠ is the breathier version of ਟ, the same pairing pattern as ਚ/ਛ and ਜ/ਝ from before. Practice saying ta... tha, feeling your tongue curl back each time.
You now know sixteen letters, and you've felt a whole new way of making a sound with your tongue! Tomorrow we'll add three more letters from this same row.

objectives: Recognize and name the letters ਟ (tainka) and ਠ (thattha)
Physically notice the tongue-curling ('retroflex') articulation that distinguishes this row
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Review the fourteen letters learned so far.
2. Introduce ਟ and ਠ, having the child physically feel their tongue curl back while saying each sound.
3. Practice ta...tha together, emphasizing the tongue-curl.
4. Trace each letter in the air before picking up a pencil.
5. Move to the worksheet: trace each letter, then write it once more.
6. Close by counting all sixteen letters learned so far.
differentiationTips: Struggling: have the child place a finger near (not in) their mouth to physically notice the tongue-curl difference from earlier sounds
Ready for more: ask the child to compare this new tongue-curl sound to the more familiar ਤ-like sound they may already know from spoken Punjabi
This is the first genuinely new articulation point introduced — worth extra repetition before moving on
teacherGuide.answerKey: This is a tracing and recognition activity — check that each traced letter roughly matches the shape shown.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: ਟ, ਠ begin a new consonant row (the retroflex series) in the Painti Akhari sequence, introducing a genuinely new articulation point after two rows of more familiar sounds. Every letter was validated against gurmukhifix's Lexicon before writing.
